## The problem

Long-lived branches let our twelve engineers drift apart. Each branch diverges further from main every day it stays open, so merges arrive as multi-file, multi-author conflicts that take hours to resolve and often introduce subtle regressions no one anticipated. Integration testing happens only at the end, right when we have the least time to fix what it finds, and by then the original author has often moved on to other work and lost the context needed to fix it quickly. We are effectively discovering whether our code works together only once a release is imminent, which is the worst possible time to learn that it doesn't.

## The proposal

I propose we adopt trunk-based development: every engineer merges small, working changes into main at least once a day, unfinished features are hidden behind flags rather than isolated on branches, and main stays releasable at all times.

- Cap branch lifetime at roughly one day; anything larger gets split into smaller, independently mergeable pieces.
- Adopt feature flags so incomplete work can sit safely in main without being exposed to users.
- Require CI to pass, including automated tests, before any merge to main is allowed.

This turns integration from a rare, painful event into a routine, low-risk one, and it gives us continuous feedback instead of a stressful surprise at release time.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection deserves a real answer: merging incomplete, flag-gated code into main more often increases the chance that a mistake reaches production, and flags themselves can pile up into a confusing, half-cleaned mess if nobody owns removing them. This is a legitimate cost, not a strawman, and it means our success depends on genuine CI discipline and a habit of retiring flags promptly — not just good intentions. If we adopt trunk-based development without that rigor, we will simply trade branch conflicts for production incidents.

- Expect a rough first month while habits and tooling catch up to the new workflow.
- Some engineers will need coaching on decomposing work into small, safely mergeable increments.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
